newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech begins wireless broadband service.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech begins wireless broadband service.

text.p: Ameritech Corp said Tuesday it launched a wireless digital broadband service that will provide customers with high-speed, door-to-door connectivity of voice, data and video.
Ameritech Wireless Broadband Service is a local loop access offering for customers who need high-speed, cost effective access to existing phone lines and fiber optic networks, it said.

"Ameritech Wireless Broadband Service enables us to provide seamless high-speed connectivity for LAN (local area network) interconnection, desktop videoconferencing and Internet access," Eric Hyde, Ameritech director of data marketing, said in a statement. "It also enables us to be a full-service communications provider for our customers."

Using 38 gigahertz microwave technology, Ameritech will be able to provide local access service for its customers as well as network diversity and back-up recovery that can be deployed quickly and inexpensively, it said.

Hyde said Ameritech plans to focus on serving its customers in the Midwest, beginning in November. He added that the technology would enable Ameritech to provide local access service for customers anywhere.

Ameritech Wireless Broadband Service will be provide through an equity-based strategic alliance with Advanced Radio Telecom Inc, which was been granted 38 gigahertz licenses thorughout the country by the U.S. Federal Communications Commission.

"The rapid growth of and demand for Internet services, LAN interconnection and videoconferencing is significantly increasing the volume of broadband traffic," Hyde said. "We want to be able to provide another option for customers who need high-speed access to external communications networks."
